items.title: Karl Berger interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, August 11, 2014

ctx.x: Yes, but we were chatting about this, the state of the world now. The news is not very good. And I wonder if that affects your thinking and your creative impulse.

Well you know our teacher, Trungpa Rinpoche, talked about the state of the world creating a genuine feeling of sadness. And that’s happening all the time actually. You know? There is the sadness of being in life or just for a few years, that you get sick and that people suffer. And you suffer for them and with them and you’re living basically in the world that generates what is called generated sadness. What he meant by genuine is that you don’t get like bogged down by it you know. Just like because people could…

experience these things and not get killed by it yourself. I was just yesterday reading this story about this Chicago recording with this guy who was so sensitive to the music and recorded everything that was played in these little clubs, and over the Iraq war he killed himself. And that’s sort of a place, you know, when you deal with the arts you’re actually trying to portray and also make people go to a world where you can actually feel the positive vibration. That’s like really prevalent. That’s like what’s…
